verdict.summary: Build a public GitHub App and distribute it through direct installation, not a Marketplace listing, for a multi-tenant agent that works in customer-selected repositories. This path is self-serve and does not require Marketplace approval; Marketplace publication is optional and is a separate listing process. GitHub does not publish a fixed Marketplace review SLA, and community reports describe variable review times.
verdict.activeEffort: 1–3 days, mostly implementing secure installation-token and webhook handling
verdict.mainGate: You must register the App under a personal account or organization you own, then each tenant must install it and choose repositories.

recommendation.text: Use a public GitHub App with installation access tokens for tenant-scoped background work. Offer GitHub App user authorization only for features that genuinely require a user context; distribute by direct installation unless Marketplace discovery or Marketplace billing is required.

sources.quote: In general, GitHub Apps are preferred over OAuth apps. GitHub Apps use fine-grained permissions, give the user more control over which repositories the app can access, and use short-lived tokens.
However, GitHub Apps can also act independently of a user.
If you set your GitHub App registration to public, any user on GitHub can install it and authorize it.

scopeTiers.text: Read a tenant-selected repository for analysis.

sources.quote: GitHub Apps don't have any permissions by default. When you register a GitHub App, you can select permissions for the app.

scopeTiers.text: Create commits or change repository content only in repositories selected during installation; no separate GitHub scope review is documented for direct public-App installation.

sources.quote: For Git operations, you should request the ‘Contents’ repository permission
Installing a GitHub App grants the app access to a user or organization account's chosen repositories.

scopeTiers.need: Agent-created commits and repository file updates

scopeTiers.text: Edit GitHub Actions workflow files only when the tenant enables that feature; add the Workflows repository permission. Direct installation remains self-serve, while Marketplace publication is a separate listing review.

sources.quote: for editing Actions workflow files, request “the ‘Workflows’ repository permission.”
Apps on GitHub Marketplace must meet the requirements outlined on this page before the listing can be published.

scopeTiers.scopes: Repository Contents: read and write; Repository Workflows: read and write

essentials.text: Create installation access tokens server-side using a GitHub App JWT. Installation tokens expire after 1 hour. If user authorization is needed, request offline_access only when necessary: the user access token expires after eight hours, the refresh token expires after six months without use, and refresh-token rotation requires atomically replacing the stored token.

sources.quote: The installation access token will expire after 1 hour.
The access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months without use.
Once you use a refresh token, that refresh token and the old access token will no longer work.

essentials.text: For GitHub App user authorization, register an exact HTTPS callback URL and disable wildcard matching. Use state and PKCE with S256 for every authorization request.

sources.quote: When wildcard matching is disabled, the redirect URL must exactly match the callback URL.
PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) is now supported and recommended for user authentication in OAuth and GitHub Apps.

Budget installation-token REST traffic for at least 5,000 requests per hour per installation. The documented non-Enterprise maximum is 12,500 requests per hour; GitHub Enterprise Cloud installations have 15,000 requests per hour.

sources.quote: GitHub Apps authenticating with an installation access token use the installation's minimum rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.

essentials.text: Not found in the sources researched
Make the GitHub App public and give tenants the installation URL. Public Apps can be installed by any GitHub user; Marketplace publication is optional rather than a production prerequisite.

sources.quote: If you set your GitHub App registration to public, any user on GitHub can install it and authorize it.
If your GitHub App is public to all users on GitHub, you can also choose to publish it to GitHub Marketplace.

essentials.text: No review is required for direct public-App installation. If you choose Marketplace publication, complete the listing requirements and select Request publish; GitHub says an onboarding expert will follow up.

sources.quote: To submit your completed app listing, click Request publish.
An onboarding expert will reach out to you with additional information.

essentials.text: Validate every webhook's X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC-SHA256 value with a high-entropy secret and constant-time comparison. Before acting, bind the webhook installation ID and repository or organization owner to the stored tenant installation record.

sources.quote: you should validate the webhook signature before processing the delivery further.
Never use a plain == operator.
Installation access tokens are limited to specified repositories with the permissions chosen by the creator of the app.

detail.text: In Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps, register the App under your personal account or an organization you own. Set it public so customer accounts and organizations can install it.

sources.quote: You can register a GitHub App under your personal account or under any organization you own.
If you set your GitHub App registration to public, any user on GitHub can install it and authorize it.

steps.title: Prepare a least-privilege permission rationale

detail.text: Use this rationale to decide the minimum repository and optional organization permissions before configuring the App.

sources.quote: GitHub Apps don't have any permissions by default. When you register a GitHub App, you can select permissions for the app.
If your app only needs ‘Administration’ permission to create repositories, request the ‘Repository creation’ permission instead.

steps.output:
Permissions rationale:
• Contents read/write: analyze and create requested repository changes.
• Workflows read/write: optional; enable only for requested Actions workflow edits.
• Organization read: optional; use only to identify authorized tenant context.
No Administration permission is requested. Each tenant selects the repositories available to the agent.

detail.text: In the App registration, add only required repository permissions, configure an exact HTTPS user-authorization callback if user-context features exist, and set a high-entropy webhook secret and required events. Do not enable wildcard callback matching.

sources.quote: When wildcard matching is disabled, the redirect URL must exactly match the callback URL.
GitHub sends an HMAC-SHA256 value in `X-Hub-Signature-256`.

detail.text: In your webhook endpoint, verify the signature before parsing or dispatching the event, then reject events whose installation ID, repository ID, or organization owner does not match the tenant installation record.

sources.quote: you should validate the webhook signature before processing the delivery further.
Never hardcode a token into an application or push a token to any repository.

steps.title: Install into a controlled test repository

detail.text: Install the App on a controlled account or organization and select only a test repository. Exercise read and write features with an installation access token limited to that repository.

sources.quote: You can list up to 500 repositories.
the installation access token will have access to all repositories that the installation was granted access to.

detail.text: Confirm that a token cannot access an unselected repository, expired installation tokens are renewed server-side, invalid webhook signatures are rejected, and tenant-mismatched installation events do nothing.

sources.quote: The installation access token cannot be granted permissions that the app was not granted.
The installation access token will expire after 1 hour.

steps.title: Skip provider review for direct public installation

detail.text: Do not submit a Marketplace listing unless you need Marketplace discovery or Marketplace billing; a public App can serve tenants through direct installation.

sources.quote: If your GitHub App is public to all users on GitHub, you can also choose to publish it to GitHub Marketplace.

detail.text: Publish the App installation link in your product, persist each installation ID with its tenant and approved repositories, and generate a new server-side installation token for each job rather than sharing tokens across tenants.

sources.quote: Installing a GitHub App grants the app access to a user or organization account's chosen repositories.
The installation access token will expire after 1 hour.

gotchas.text: Do not use an OAuth App with the repo scope as the default authorization model for repository-writing automation: repo grants broad access to public and private repositories and related resources.

sources.quote: Grants full access to public and private repositories including read and write access to code, commit statuses, repository invitations, collaborators, deployment statuses, and repository webhooks.

gotchas.text: Never use Smee in production because its channels are not authenticated or secure.

sources.quote: Never use Smee for an application in production. Smee channels are not authenticated or secure.

gotchas.text: Avoid bulk collection of public GitHub content for commercial AI-model training without legal review; GitHub's AI-specific automated-access terms are distinct from customer-authorized repository work.

sources.quote: By using automated means to access, collect, or otherwise use (‘Access’) any publicly accessible Content from the Service for the purpose of developing or training any commercially available artificial intelligence model,

gotchas.text: Marketplace billing is materially different from direct installation: paid plans require a verified publisher and GitHub says paid GitHub Apps should have a minimum of 100 installations.

sources.quote: To publish a paid plan for your app on the GitHub Marketplace, your app must be owned by an organization that is a verified publisher.
should have a minimum of 100 installations.

whenBlocked.text: If an App configuration, installation, webhook delivery, or Marketplace issue cannot be resolved, open a GitHub Support ticket at https://support.github.com/ with the App slug or ID, listing URL if applicable, timestamps, failed delivery or request IDs, and redacted logs.

sources.quote: Use the GitHub Support portal to contact GitHub Support when you need help troubleshooting issues.

whenBlocked.text: If a customer needs a permission not granted to the App, change the App registration only after evaluating the feature, then ask the customer to approve the resulting updated permission request; installation tokens cannot elevate permissions on their own.
